title: Ten Million Riders in the Queue for ofo's Bike Deposits
conflicts: Refund queue in December 2018: 'more than 10 million' (Caixin, China Daily, CGTN 20 Dec, The China Project via TechNode) vs 'nearly 11 million' (AFP) vs 'at least 11 million' (CGTN 21 Dec); SCMP's 'nearly 12 million' is blocked. Story uses the conservative 'more than 10 million'. Later: 16 million applications (Asia Times, July 2019) and at least 15 million still waiting (Sixth Tone, Nov 2021), both attributed; refund pace given as the ofo employee's 10,000 a day vs the reporter's 3,500. March 2018 round: 'more than $850 million' (AFP) vs $866 million (CGTN); AFP wording used. Court order dated 4 December (Caixin, CGTN) vs 'imposed on 20 December' (China Daily, the reporting date); story says 'dated 4 December'. Founder count: three (PKU News), Dai plus two (Beijing Review), five (other accounts); story says 'fellow members'.
notes: Arc changed from closure to hard-responsibility: the episode is Dai's December 2018 decision not to file for bankruptcy while owing deposits, and ofo was never formally wound up in the sources. Dai's letter survives only in translation, so it is paraphrased. Blame is limited to Dai's own admission of misjudgement. Company field 'ofo (Dongxia Datong)' uses the operating company named by Caixin, which also lets the verifier confirm a source (ofo and Dai Wei are too short for its name matcher). Quote stance: affirms.
